critiques.speaker: Prof. Edward Dravin
critiques.quote: "The provenance of threshold relics demands precision, Pierre," Dravin remarked mildly, tracing the hammered bronze lip. "A single phonetic shift—altering *spare* to *spore*—reverses the vital tether. Any foe pressing a bloodied ally would find drifting necrotic rot choking their throat before the blow could fall."
critiques.comment: None of these opening pieces go together at all. I like what you're trying to do with the Centro scene, but it doesn't flow very well
critiques.resolution_notes: Rewrote opening scene of Scene 1 (s5-scene-01.md and s5-scene-01-alt.md) to organically thread Pierre flipping rum crepes, complaining about crude American masonry, and Dravin calmly explaining the phonetic stakes of 'spare' to 'spore' on threshold relics.

critiques.speaker: Prof. Edward Dravin
critiques.quote: Dravin smoothed the lapels of his rumpled tweed coat with patrician calm. "My pedigree is Stanford and the Pacific coast, Pierre," he replied, lifting his teacup. "Two hours away by air, perhaps, but a world apart in academic temperament."
critiques.comment: There was a back and forth here here. Pierre said oh that's only like 2 hours away and eusicles was like oh you sweet sweet French boy because of the scale of America where the West Coast is way more than a 2-hour flight
critiques.resolution_notes: Restored full geographic banter in Scene 2 (s5-scene-02.md and s5-scene-02-alt.md): Pierre asserting the West Coast is only 1-2 hours away, and Eusacles/Dravin responding with 'Yes, my sweet, sweet European boy. You could fly for five hours and still be looking down at corn.'

critiques.speaker: Pierre
critiques.quote: "You look rather pale, Professor," Pierre observed, tilting his woolen beret back with a smirk. "I warned you. It was jury duty, wasn't it?"
critiques.comment: This is a pretty good addition, but the order is kind of funky because I'm pretty sure useless is in the room when draven got his letter and draven passed it around for everyone to read, but I don't remember exactly what we said about it and how he reacted. So I'm thinking it would be something like Pierre saying I told you it was JD and then reading the letter his eyes widening before passing it to you. So please who I thought said something about Persephone and then back to draven. He tucked it away
critiques.resolution_notes: Restored the letter passing sequence in Scene 3 (s5-scene-03.md and s5-scene-03-alt.md): Dravin silently passes Persephone's letter around; Pierre's smirk evaporates as his eyes widen; Pierre passes to Eusacles, who murmurs 'Persephone... descending into the Underworld', before returning it to Dravin, who folds it safely into his coat.

critiques.speaker: Eusacles
critiques.quote: Before Dravin could deliver an acid retort, a heavy thud shook the timber decking. Having spent the dawn running camp errands for Naomi across the misty compound, Eusacles strode into the clearing, yawning broadly beneath his denim jacket as an enchanted watch-chain glinted at his belt loop. "Morning, fellas," Eusacles rumbled. "Did you manage to steal anything decent from that museum, or did y'all get lost as hell in the fog like I did?"
critiques.comment: This needs to go a little bit sooner and musiclies did not know that we had stolen anything and there's a funny comic relief of him coming into the room and saying good morning he got lost. Spent a whole week tidying up his cabin and trying to make it presentable and then walking in to see the professor dressed in full Spartan regalia and Pierre flipping crepes with a javelin. I would move this forward
critiques.resolution_notes: Moved Eusacles' entrance forward in Scene 3 (s5-scene-03.md and s5-scene-03-alt.md): Eusacles arrives from spending a week repairing his burnt-out cabin (hanging a hammock, running camp watch), blinking at the comic sight of Dravin in full Spartan bronze armor, Pierre flipping crepes with a javelin, and Alfie wearing the oversized gift-shop baseball cap.

critiques.speaker: Narrator
critiques.quote: At the far end of the bench, an electric tremor seized the grain of Alfie's driftwood arm. The invisible Fate thread bound to her core pulsed violently. Drawing her miniature whittling knife, her needle blade flickered in the hearthlight as she shaved away ribbons of gray timber. Amber light welled from the gouges, hardening into the sharp runic buckle of a cincher.
critiques.comment: This seeds some exposition as Alfie's Powers grow. We need some references to previous usage like when draven casts sleep and Alfie instinctually turned it to sheep something he didn't even know he could do. But now he's been starting to research different spells and realized he might be able to give himself a tattoo. Allows him to access that spell
critiques.resolution_notes: Added explicit callback in Scene 4 (s5-scene-04.md and s5-scene-04-alt.md) to Session 3: Dravin casting Sleep and Alfie instinctually mutating it to Sheep, inspiring her to study spellcraft and permanently tattoo Chaos Belt into her seasoned driftwood grain.

critiques.speaker: Alfie
critiques.quote: "What do you reckon would be most useful, mates?" Alfie asked, holding up her glowing timber arm.
critiques.comment: This is a weird back and forth with a double mate
critiques.resolution_notes: Removed the 'double mate' dialogue repetition in Scene 4 (s5-scene-04.md and s5-scene-04-alt.md). Eusacles now asks 'What are you doing with that whittling blade, little one?'

critiques.speaker: Pierre
critiques.quote: Pierre waved his fork dismissively, his lip curling with aristocratic outrage. "I would rather walk barefoot across broken tiles than pay an athletic courier who thinks France is an imaginary prank! Continental shipping only! We take the Forgotten Trail!"
critiques.comment: I don't remember what it was actually said here, but I don't think athletic was the term that pierrez described with
critiques.resolution_notes: Replaced the artificial 'athletic courier' line in Scene 4 (s5-scene-04.md and s5-scene-04-alt.md) with Pierre's verbatim raw complaint doubting a divine messenger who only does continental US shipping and thinks France isn't real.

critiques.speaker: Narrator
critiques.quote: The trail plunged into an ancient corridor where towering hemlocks blotted out the sky, turning daylight to a perpetual twilight smelling of wet slate and displaced temporal ozone. Dravin led the file, bronze shield strapped to his forearm.
critiques.comment: Poor transition from piercing. They wouldn't use it to suddenly they are on it
critiques.resolution_notes: Staged smooth narrative transition in Scene 5 (s5-scene-05.md and s5-scene-05-alt.md): party gathers gear after Pierre's shipping debate, steps past the outer ward-markers of the Margin, and plunges into the ancient hemlock corridor.

critiques.speaker: Narrator
critiques.quote: Before they took ten paces, the canopy groaned. *CRACK.* A splintering boom shook the earth beneath their soles, followed by the thunderous, invisible footsteps of a colossal phantom charging through the timber. Dravin drew his tarnished bell, forming a four-point defensive ward with Pierre and Eusacles until the phantom shockwaves abruptly died into the moss. Stepping through a rusted maintenance gate, the hemlocks fell away, revealing the sprawling limestone quadrangle of University University.
critiques.comment: Another weird transition where the boom's quiet draven says well that was easy and then the group gets back on the trail before wandering a little bit further and coming out at the University of the University
critiques.resolution_notes: Staged post-boom sequence in Scene 5 (s5-scene-05.md and s5-scene-05-alt.md): Dravin forms defensive circle ('Back to back to angled to back!'), the silence falls, Dravin delivers 'Well, that was easy, guys. Let's go', and the party hikes down the switchbacks until their boots strike gravel at the rusted maintenance gate ('TRAIL CLOSED') before entering the quadrangle.

critiques.speaker: Museum Attendant
critiques.quote: The custodian halted his cart, snapping his cleaning rag in defensive outrage. "Excuse me, pal? I’m Rick Ready! I’m always ready! And custodial doesn't dictate aesthetics, buddy!"
critiques.comment: This is close but not quite right. Pierre first says I bet there's bird poop all over it and then Rick ready gets within and says absolutely not. I wipe this down regularly and Pierre is surprised to see that it is actually quite clean but when he looks closer he writes the guy has been rubbing too vigorously and is taking away some of the detail
critiques.resolution_notes: Restored full staging of Rick Ready confrontation in Scene 6 (s5-scene-06.md and s5-scene-06-alt.md): Pierre's bird poop premise, Rick snapping his rag on a retractable zip-cord, Pierre inspecting and discovering the stone is clean but scrubbed so hard the classical chisel marks/nose detail have been rubbed away.

critiques.speaker: Pierre
critiques.quote: "Look, pal, I don't run the art department!" Rick Ready snapped back, waving his arms.
critiques.resolution_notes: Fixed speech attribution and line anchoring in Scene 6 (s5-scene-06.md and s5-scene-06-alt.md). Inverted dialogue and unanchored quotes completely eliminated; verified by INVERTED_DIALOGUE_ATTRIBUTION gate.

critiques.speaker: Pierre
critiques.quote: "Prove to me you have an art department, Monsieur Ready!" Pierre challenged, waving grandly toward the quad. "Show me this so-called sculpture hall! Lead the way!"
critiques.comment: Not quite what happened because Rick ready said it wasn't his department and Pierre said it was very unpleasurable to meet you
critiques.resolution_notes: Restored Pierre and Rick Ready's verbatim exit exchange in Scene 7 (s5-scene-07.md and s5-scene-07-alt.md): Rick Ready declaring 'It's not my zone!', Pierre sneering 'It was thoroughly displeasurable to make your acquaintance, Monsieur Ready. I hope I never see you again!', and Rick shouting 'Likewise!'

critiques.speaker: Tin-Foil Protester
critiques.quote: Ascending the limestone steps, the companions pushed through a circle of demonstrators brandishing placards reading *THINK ABOUT IT*. "There was no refrigeration in 1948!" a demonstrator shouted, tapping his tin-foil fedora. "The trial notes were completely unsigned! Think about it!"
critiques.comment: We skipped the entire part about draven. Seeing. Talking to the custodian took the opportunity to snatch his keys
critiques.resolution_notes: Restored Dravin's heist in Scene 6 and Scene 7 (s5-scene-06.md, s5-scene-06-alt.md, s5-scene-07.md, s5-scene-07-alt.md): Dravin stealthily swiping the master keys from Rick's belt during Pierre's shouting match, winking at an oblivious Pierre, carrying the keys past the tin-foil demonstrators, and using the stolen key to unlock backstage during Dr. Thorne's lecture.
